nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Life below water|Species conservation|Species population surveys
nodes.label: Species population surveys

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Life below water|Species conservation|Species population surveys_qna_000
nodes.label: Facts
nodes.question: How many survey points were established in each of the reference sites?
nodes.answer: 10 survey points were established in each of the two reference sites, totaling 20 survey points.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Life below water|Species conservation|Species population surveys_qna_001
nodes.label: Science and tech
nodes.question: How many tagged colonies were sampled for the study?
nodes.answer: Five tagged colonies were sampled at each study site.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Life below water|Species conservation|Species population surveys_qna_002
nodes.label: Science and tech
nodes.question: What type of data was used in the study to test the interaction of guild traits with populations and habitats?
nodes.answer: The study used population abundance data collected from a community of amphibians and reptiles combined with guild factors from known life history information.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Life below water|Species conservation|Species population surveys_qna_003
nodes.label: Methodology
nodes.question: What methods were used for primary data collection in the study?
nodes.answer: The primary data collection methods included questionnaire surveys and semi-structured questionnaire surveys.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Life below water|Species conservation|Species population surveys_qna_004
nodes.label: Facts
nodes.question: How much have kangaroo populations in South-East Queensland declined since 2000?
nodes.answer: Kangaroo populations in South-East Queensland have estimated declines of up to ~ 40% since 2000.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Life below water|Species conservation|Species population surveys_qna_005
nodes.label: Facts
nodes.question: How many species of smaller felids were assessed in the study?
nodes.answer: Seven species of smaller felids were assessed in the study.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Life below water|Species conservation|Species population surveys_qna_006
nodes.label: Management
nodes.question: What procedure was used once an incubating northern lapwing nest was located?
nodes.answer: A spring trap was placed on the nest after flushing the individuals, and once trapped, they were ringed, weighed, and photographed to determine sex after release.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Life below water|Species conservation|Species population surveys_qna_007
nodes.label: Facts
nodes.question: Over which time periods were nest surveys conducted for northern lapwing pairs in 2022 and 2023?
nodes.answer: Nest surveys were conducted from early April to mid-May 2022 and from early April to mid-June 2023.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Life below water|Species conservation|Species population surveys_qna_008
nodes.label: Ecology
nodes.question: Which authors contributed to the understanding of metapopulations and source-sink dynamics?
nodes.answer: Hanski (1999) contributed to metapopulation understanding, while Pulliam (1988) and Dias (1992) contributed to the understanding of source-sink dynamics.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Life below water|Species conservation|Species population surveys_qna_009
nodes.label: Science and tech
nodes.question: What specific measurements were taken from the birds during the study?
nodes.answer: The specific measurements taken from the birds included weight, wing length, and tarsus length.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Life below water|Species conservation|Species population surveys_qna_010
nodes.label: Facts
nodes.question: How many sites did the researchers collect acoustic data from during the study?
nodes.answer: The researchers collected acoustic data from sixty-one sites.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Life below water|Species conservation|Species population surveys_qna_011
nodes.label: Facts
nodes.question: How many swift parrots were estimated to remain as of the latest report?
nodes.answer: Fewer than 500 individuals remain.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Life below water|Species conservation|Species population surveys_qna_012
nodes.label: Facts
nodes.question: How many study sites were acoustic data collected from in Cyprus?
nodes.answer: Acoustic data were collected from sixty-one study sites in Cyprus.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Life below water|Species conservation|Species population surveys_qna_013
nodes.label: Science and tech
nodes.question: What potential task can CLAP perform that was previously unattainable with supervised bioacoustic approaches?
nodes.answer: CLAP has the potential to estimate relative distances and discover unknown animal species.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Life below water|Species conservation|Species population surveys_qna_014
nodes.label: Science and tech
nodes.question: What has been the impact of ARUs on data collection for sound-producing animals?
nodes.answer: The applications of ARUs are expanding, enabling projects to amass and analyze hundreds of thousands of audio recordings that were previously difficult to collect.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Life below water|Species conservation|Species population surveys_qna_015
nodes.label: Science and tech
nodes.question: What was the timeframe of the occurrence location collection for D. rotundus in the study?
nodes.answer: The occurrence locations of D. rotundus were collected from 1901 to 2023.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Life below water|Species conservation|Species population surveys_qna_016
nodes.label: Science and tech
nodes.question: What is the main purpose of the pilot study discussed in the paragraph?
nodes.answer: The main purpose of the pilot study is to test the performance of a non-invasive monitoring strategy for terrestrial small mammals and to gather data on their distribution in relation to climate change and biodiversity loss.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Life below water|Species conservation|Species population surveys_qna_017
nodes.label: Science and tech
nodes.question: What percentage of samples were successfully processed for molecular species identification, and how many could be assigned to a specific species?
nodes.answer: COI-PCR products were obtained from 93% of samples, and 55% of those could be assigned to a small mammal species based on high-quality Sanger-Sequences.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Life below water|Species conservation|Species population surveys_qna_018
nodes.label: Science and tech
nodes.question: Which groups of small mammals were identified in the study, and which species were dominant in local communities?
nodes.answer: The study identified 11 species from the groups Eulipotyphla and Rodentia, with local communities being dominated by Apodemus sp. and Clethrionomys glareolus.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Life below water|Species conservation|Species population surveys_qna_019
nodes.label: Regulation
nodes.question: What does the Habitats Directive of 1992 mandate regarding population trends in Europe?
nodes.answer: The Habitats Directive of 1992 mandates that an assessment of population trends is mandatory for many species of conservation concern.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Life below water|Species conservation|Species population surveys_qna_020
nodes.label: Science and tech
nodes.question: Which species' feces were collected non-invasively using Mouse Bait Stations?
nodes.answer: Feces from small mammals, specifically mentioned in the context of the usage of Mouse Bait Stations, were collected non-invasively.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Life below water|Species conservation|Species population surveys_qna_021
nodes.label: Science and tech
nodes.question: What is the main focus of the methodological approach described in the paragraph?
nodes.answer: The main focus is on large-scale species assessment based on fecal pellets as a DNA source and COI barcodes as molecular markers, particularly for small mammals.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Life below water|Species conservation|Species population surveys_qna_022
nodes.label: Methods
nodes.question: What sampling methods were used to collect benthic invertebrate samples?
nodes.answer: Standardized multi-habitat sampling methods were used to collect benthic invertebrate samples.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Life below water|Species conservation|Species population surveys_qna_023
nodes.question: What significant trend regarding vertebrate populations was documented in the Living Planet Report 2022?
nodes.answer: The report documents an average 69% decline in the relative abundance of monitored wildlife populations around the world between 1970 and 2018.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Life below water|Species conservation|Species population surveys_qna_024
nodes.question: How significant is the decline in vertebrate populations according to the Living Planet Report?
nodes.answer: The report shows an average decline of 69% in the relative abundance of monitored wildlife populations globally between 1970 and 2018. Latin America has experienced the greatest decline at 94%.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Life below water|Species conservation|Species population surveys_qna_025
nodes.question: What significant trend regarding global wildlife populations does the Living Planet Report 2022 highlight?
nodes.answer: The report highlights an average decline of 69% in the relative abundance of monitored wildlife populations globally between 1970 and 2018, with Latin America showing a 94% decline and freshwater species populations experiencing an 83% decline.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Life below water|Species conservation|Species population surveys_qna_026
nodes.question: What average decline in relative abundance of monitored freshwater populations was reported between 1970 and 2016?
nodes.answer: The average decline in relative abundance of monitored freshwater populations was 83% between 1970 and 2016.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Life below water|Species conservation|Species population surveys_qna_027
nodes.question: What is the average decline in monitored populations according to the 2022 global Living Planet Index?
nodes.answer: The average decline in monitored populations between 1970 and 2018 is 69%.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Life below water|Species conservation|Species population surveys_qna_028
nodes.question: What percentage decline in monitored freshwater populations was reported between 1970 and 2016 according to the freshwater Living Planet Index?
nodes.answer: An average decline of 76% was reported in monitored freshwater populations between 1970 and 2016.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Life below water|Species conservation|Species population surveys_qna_029
nodes.question: What percentage decline in monitored populations does the Living Planet Index report for freshwater populations since 1970?
nodes.answer: The Living Planet Index reports an average decline of 83% in monitored freshwater populations since 1970.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Life below water|Species conservation|Species population surveys_qna_030
nodes.question: What is the average decline in populations recorded by the Freshwater Living Planet Index?
nodes.answer: The average decline in populations recorded by the Freshwater Living Planet Index is 83% between 1970 and 2016.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Life below water|Species conservation|Species population surveys_qna_031
nodes.question: What does the Freshwater Living Planet Index reveal about the average decline of populations from 1970 to 2016?
nodes.answer: The Freshwater Living Planet Index shows an average decline of 76% in monitored freshwater populations from 1970 to 2016.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Life below water|Species conservation|Species population surveys_qna_032
nodes.label: Facts
nodes.question: How many residents participated in the online survey for the study?
nodes.answer: A total of 850 residents participated in the online survey.
